title: The nine long vowels
summary: The long vowels by tongue position, as an IPA chart. Each cell gives the sound; find its letter.

o.note: Long o is usually /uː/. In some words it is /oː/, the sound of å: sova "sleep".

u.note: A close vowel made far forward, with the lips pressed together rather than pushed out; Engstrand (1990) places it near the front. Short u is /ɵ/: full.

ae.note: Before r it opens to /æː/: är "is".

oe.note: Before r it opens to /œː/: öra "ear".
